title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BOBBIE'S GARAGE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Bobbie Kane, who mixes paint at a hardware store in Bend, Oregon.
She can match any color. But she could not find the floor of her own garage.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE AVALANCHE
segments.quote: How many things I can do without!
segments.author: Socrates
lines: The kids were grown, so Bobbie and her husband Doug wanted a little cabin.
The real estate lady opened their garage, and four hundred plastic lids fell on her. No bottoms.
At work, Bobbie's coworker Hector had a line from Socrates taped to the register:
How many things I can do without!
That Saturday, Bobbie found three waffle irons. She kept one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FOURTEEN LAMPS
segments.quote: It is preoccupation with possessions, more than anything else, that prevents men from living freely and nobly.
segments.author: Bertrand Russell
lines: Next came fourteen broken lamps. I'll fix them someday, she said. For twenty years.
Her daughter Kayla read her a line from Bertrand Russell, the British thinker:
It is preoccupation with possessions, more than anything else, that prevents men from living freely and nobly.
So Bobbie held a yard sale. One man bought all fourteen lamps. He fixes lamps.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE TROPHY BOXES
segments.quote: One can collect only a few, and they are more beautiful if they are few.
segments.author: Anne Morrow Lindbergh
lines: Then the hard boxes. The kids' trophies. Every birthday card ever.
Her mom's old copy of Gift from the Sea, by Anne Morrow Lindbergh, had a page folded down:
One can collect only a few, and they are more beautiful if they are few.
So she framed the five best cards. Doug kept one trophy. Bowling. Fourth place.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: MOVING DAY
segments.quote: Loss is nothing else than change. But the universal nature delights in change.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: On moving day, Bobbie stood in the empty living room and cried. Thirty-one Thanksgivings happened there.
Doug read from the little book in his lunch box, by Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor:
Loss is nothing else than change. But the universal nature delights in change.
She locked the door and didn't look back. Well, maybe once.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE FOURTH WAFFLE IRON
segments.quote: He who knows that enough is enough will always have enough.
segments.author: Lao Tzu
lines: A week later, Bobbie saw a shiny new waffle iron on sale. Her hand reached out by itself.
Then she remembered Kayla's kitchen calendar, from Lao Tzu, the old Chinese teacher:
He who knows that enough is enough will always have enough.
She bought pancake mix instead.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: TWELVE FOLDING CHAIRS
segments.quote: Of all the means which wisdom acquires to ensure happiness throughout the whole of life, by far the most important is friendship.
segments.author: Epicurus
lines: That Thanksgiving, the cabin had two rooms, one couch and twelve folding chairs.
Hector came. The lamp man came. Knees touched under the table.
Doug raised his glass to Epicurus, the Greek thinker:
Of all the means which wisdom acquires to ensure happiness throughout the whole of life, by far the most important is friendship.
The old house had room for everything. The cabin had room for everybody.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do without. Let go. Keep a few. Accept change. Know enough. Make room for friends.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do without. Let go. Keep a few. Accept change. Know enough. Make room for friends.
Me? I own seven bow ties. I need two. Don't tell anyone.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
